title: SQLite schema drift: a boolean field declaring defaultValue 'false' (a string) is reported as set_column_default drift on every read, and re-applying it changes nothing
body:
repo:objectstack#5 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CbdHk3orAeensH6EzS

Filing gate: ① · Source: fleet (os-dev measurement on PR #37425 for #37345, report comment 7182686626) · finding class a · reach: named producer (`SqlDriver.detectManagedDrift`: the boot drift warning and `os migrate plan`, on any SQLite datasource).

Grading: `area:data` · Bug · measured at PR #37425 head `f438ff8c` through both `driver-turso` faces; not introduced by that PR (the local face has written `'0'` since before it) · evidence: measured.
Suggested-grade: p3 · a permanent false drift entry; no data is wrong, but the drift report never goes clean for such a field and a re-apply loops.

## What

A `boolean` field declaring `defaultValue: 'false'` (a string) gets column DEFAULT `'0'` (knex's boolean formatter on the local face; the shared renderer on the remote face after PR #37425). `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/schema-drift.ts` `physicalLiteralMatches` compares a string declaration as text, so it reports `default_mismatch` / `set_column_default` (expected DEFAULT `'false'`, actual DEFAULT `'0'`) on every read, and applying the entry writes `'0'` again.

## Acceptance (proposed, for triage)

- The differ normalises a boolean declaration the way the writer renders it (`'false'` / `false` → `0`, a truthy value → `1`, for `boolean` and `toggle` columns), so a freshly synced column reads zero drift on both faces.
- `turso-remote-default-parity.test.ts`'s separate `'false'` describe joins the per-kind zero-drift set; the docblock note pointing here goes.

Related: #37345 (PR #37425), #36245 (local DEFAULT drift).
Dedupe: searched 'physicalLiteralMatches', 'set_column_default boolean', 'default_mismatch boolean' — no open card.
